recipes.title: Vietnamese tofu noodle salad, light
recipes.summary: Cool rice noodles, golden tofu and crisp vegetables tossed with a bright lime, soy and sesame dressing. Extra vegetables and less noodles and oil keep this vegan dinner light.

steps.instruction: Prepare the tofu, cucumber, carrot, bean sprouts, spring onions, cilantro and garlic in their listed forms.
Stir the lime, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic and sesame oil into a smooth dressing.
Coat the tofu with one third of the dressing and leave it to absorb the seasoning.
Cook the rice noodles until tender but still springy.
Rinse the rice noodles under cold water and drain them thoroughly.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Cook the tofu until golden on several sides.
Combine the rice noodles, cucumber, carrot and bean sprouts in a large bowl.
Top the noodle salad with the tofu, spring onions and cilantro.
Pour the remaining dressing over the Vietnamese tofu noodle salad.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled shortly before serving. Refrigerate the tofu, noodles, vegetables and dressing separately for up to 3 days. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Chinese spring onion pancakes, light
recipes.summary: Flaky Chinese pancakes layered with spring onions and sesame oil, then pan-fried until crisp. Less flour and oil keep this vegetarian breakfast lighter.

steps.instruction: Mix the wheat flour, water and half the salt into a shaggy dough.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic.
Rest the dough covered so the wheat flour hydrates fully.
Prepare the spring onions in their listed form.
Divide the dough into four equal pieces.
Roll each dough piece into a thin rectangle.
Brush each rectangle lightly with the sesame oil.
Scatter the spring onions and remaining salt over the dough.
Roll each rectangle into a tight coil.
Rest the coils so the dough relaxes.
Flatten each coil into a round pancake.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan.
Cook the first sides of the pancakes until crisp and golden.
Turn the pancakes carefully.
Cook the second sides until golden and the layers are cooked through.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten freshly fried. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a dry pan or hot oven. Freeze cooked pancakes for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: French salmon leek gratin, light
recipes.summary: Tender salmon, potatoes and leeks baked in a light thyme cream sauce beneath a little parmesan. Extra leeks keep this French lunch generous but lighter.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the salmon, potato, leek and garlic in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until just tender while the slices still hold their shape.
Melt the butter in a wide frying pan.
Cook the leek until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir until fragrant.
Arrange the potato across the base of a baking dish.
Spread the leek evenly over the potato.
Place the salmon over the leek.
Whisk the heavy cream, whole milk, lemon juice and salt together.
Pour the cream mixture evenly into the baking dish.
Scatter the parmesan cheese over the gratin.
Bake until the salmon is cooked and the sauce is bubbling and lightly golden.
Rest the French salmon leek gratin before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat covered until the salmon is hot. Freezing is not recommended because the cream sauce and potatoes can separate.

recipes.title: Greek chicken souvlaki with lemon potatoes, light
recipes.summary: Grilled chicken souvlaki with peppers and onions, roasted lemon potatoes and cool cucumber yogurt. Less potato and oil keep this high-protein Greek dinner lighter.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the chicken breast, potato, cucumber, bell pepper, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Mix the lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, paprika, thyme and salt into a marinade.
Coat the chicken breast with half the marinade.
Marinate the chicken breast in the refrigerator.
Coat the potato with the remaining marinade.
Roast the potato until nearly tender and golden underneath.
Thread the chicken breast, bell pepper and onion onto skewers.
Turn the potato wedges so they brown evenly.
Grill the first sides of the skewers until browned and lightly charred.
Turn the skewers.
Grill until the chicken breast is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Stir the greek yogurt with the cucumber.
Rest the chicken souvlaki so the breast stays juicy.
Serve the Greek chicken souvlaki with the lemon potatoes and yogurt.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the chicken, potatoes and cucumber yogurt separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and potatoes until hot. Freeze the cooked chicken for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Spanish tortilla with spinach, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Spanish tortilla with tender potatoes, sweet onion and plenty of spinach bound with softly cooked eggs. Less oil and potato keep the breakfast generous.

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, onion and spinach in their listed forms.
Heat most of the olive oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Cook the potato and onion gently until tender without becoming crisp.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted and its moisture evaporates.
Beat the eggs with the salt until evenly combined.
Fold the potato, onion and spinach into the eggs.
Rest the tortilla mixture so the potato absorbs some egg.
Heat the remaining olive oil in the frying pan.
Pour the tortilla mixture into the pan.
Cook the first side over low heat until the edges are set and the centre is mostly firm.
Invert the tortilla onto a large plate.
Cook the second side until set and lightly golden.
Rest the Spanish tortilla with spinach before slicing.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and serve cold, at room temperature or gently reheated. Freezing is not recommended because the potato texture becomes watery.

recipes.title: Spanish tortilla with spinach, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Spanish tortilla with extra eggs and potatoes, sweet onion and plenty of spinach. The thick, golden breakfast is substantial and easy to share.

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, onion and spinach in their listed forms.
Heat most of the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan.
Cook the potato and onion gently until very tender and golden at the edges.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted and its moisture evaporates.
Beat the eggs with the salt until fully combined.
Fold the potato, onion and spinach into the eggs.
Rest the tortilla mixture so the larger amount of potato absorbs the egg.
Heat the remaining olive oil in the frying pan.
Pour the tortilla mixture into the pan.
Cook the first side over low heat until the thick centre is nearly set.
Invert the tortilla onto a large plate.
Cook the second side until golden and set to your liking.
Rest the Spanish tortilla with spinach before cutting generous slices.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and serve at room temperature or gently reheated. The tortilla is not suitable for freezing.
